title: SlipX tyre parameter set
description:
One (compound, surface) pair. Referenced from dynamics.yaml, never embedded in it (SCH-05).

The parameter list is the whole thesis of the project in one file: every entry is identifiable from a manoeuvre drivable in a car park with the sensors already on a competition car. Full Pacejka 5.2 is not the target, because a parameter nobody can identify is worse than one that does not exist: it gets guessed and then trusted.

The linear block is consumed from L1; the friction, mf_lite and relaxation blocks are consumed from L2 and are ignored by tiers that cannot use them.

surface.description: The surface these numbers were obtained on. Carrying coefficients across surfaces is the error the reference structure exists to prevent.

nominal_load.description: Vertical load these coefficients were identified at, per tyre. [N] Required for load sensitivity to mean anything: k_mu is an exponent about this load.

linear.description: The L1 parameters. Cornering stiffness is per TYRE, not per axle, so the file is a property of the tyre rather than of the car that happens to be wearing it; the axle value an L1 model needs is the sum over that axle's tyres.

c_alpha.description: Cornering stiffness per tyre at the nominal load, positive. [N/rad] The restoring sign lives in the force law, Fy = -C_alpha * alpha (ISO 8855), not in the parameter. Identifiable from the low-slip region of a skidpad.

c_kappa.description: Longitudinal slip stiffness per tyre at the nominal load, positive: the initial slope of longitudinal force against slip ratio. [N per unit slip] Identifiable from encoder slip ratio against IMU longitudinal acceleration in a straight-line run. Consumed from L2; a file without it loads for L0 and L1 and is refused, by name, for L2 (ADR-0025).

mu_y0.description: Peak lateral friction coefficient at the nominal load. [-] Identifiable from circle-to-slip. Values above 1.5 are physically possible for a soft sponge tyre on carpet but are more often a load or a units error, which is what the plausibility warning checks.

mu_x0.description: Peak longitudinal friction coefficient at the nominal load. [-] Identifiable from straight-line acceleration.

k_mu.description: Load sensitivity exponent: mu = mu_0 * (Fz / Fz_nominal)^(-k_mu). [-] Identifiable from a skidpad run at two ballast configurations, which is why it is in the list and Pacejka's several load-dependence terms are not. Used from L2.

mf_lite.description: Reduced Magic Formula shape factors (CORE-06, L2). Fy = mu * Fz * sin(C * atan(B * alpha - E * (B * alpha - atan(B * alpha)))). C and E are identifiable from a full slip sweep. B is DERIVED from cornering stiffness and the static load and is never consumed from this file (ADR-0023); when stated anyway it is cross-checked against the derived value and a disagreement is a named warning.

B.description: Stiffness factor. [-] Optional and never consumed: the model derives B = c_alpha / (C * mu_y0 * Fz) so that MF-lite reproduces the linear tyre exactly at small slip (ADR-0023).

C.description: Shape factor. Around 1.3 to 1.8 for lateral force; values below 1 give a curve with no peak, which is not a tyre.

E.description: Curvature factor. [-] Must not exceed 1: above it the Magic Formula is no longer monotonic up to its peak and the curve folds back on itself.

sigma.description: Relaxation length: the distance the tyre must roll for lateral force to reach 63% of its steady value. [m] Identifiable from the step-steer transient. Of the order of the contact patch length, so a value larger than the wheel circumference is a mistake.
